title: Vietnam Cement Association proposes government support to drive up self-generated power usage to cut costs and support exports
summary: Vietnam Cement Association proposes government support to drive up self-generated power usage to cut costs and support exports
body_markdown:
**Vietnam:** Luong Duc Long, the Secretary General of the Vietnam Cement Association, has proposed that the government offer support to cement producers to increase rates of self-generated power. He has recommended priority bank loans with state interest support, permission for solar and wind on assigned land, including quarries, and support from the Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry, according to the View Nam News newspaper. Long noted that raising the rate of self-generated ‘clean’ power would be cheaper for cement producers and would help exporters with carbon taxes such as the European Union’s Cross Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).


Long reported that electricity accounts for about 15 - 17% of cement production costs in the country but that electricity from the national grid contributes about 4 - 6% of production greenhouse gas emissions. He said that weak domestic demand from 2015 - 2023 left many cement plants with low profits or losses. Permitting issues have also made it difficult to convert land designated for cement plants or quarries for solar or wind projects instead. By the end of 2026, 45 of the 67 production lines in the country required to invest in waste heat recovery (WHR) systems will start operating, with a total capacity of about 320MW. Another 22 lines are investing or will invest by 2030, with a potential additional WHR capacity of about 150MW.
